body:
Both from the tensor sweep, both with existing instrumentation.

(1) RoundToHalfF32 ranges over src and indexes dst, and the compiler cannot see the documented len(dst) >= len(src) precondition, so every store carried a bounds check. One entry reslice states it once: BenchmarkRoundToHalfF32Varied -8.3 percent, with the BCE diagnostic confirming the two per-element IsInBounds gone and a single IsSliceInBounds left. Runs per element, per parameter tensor, per optimizer step on the AMP master-to-compute sync. The only behavior change — a too-short dst, already a documented programming error, panics at entry rather than mid-loop — is pinned by a test that also asserts values are unchanged for a correctly sized dst and that its own fixture actually changes under a half round-trip.

(2) gatherHalfTyped tested srcBF per ELEMENT though the half flavour is fixed before the walk. Splitting the arms so each is straight-line, and reslicing each destination run to drop the store bounds check, gave -17.2 and -16.6 percent on the two StridedCast cells.

THE OBVIOUS HOIST IS A PESSIMIZATION AND WAS MEASURED FIRST: selecting the decoder into a function value ran +51.0 and +66.5 percent. It converts a direct inlinable call into an indirect one, which costs far more than the well-predicted branch it removes. Duplicating the arms keeps the calls direct. Cast as rule HOIST-A-BRANCH-BY-DUPLICATING-NOT-BY-A-FUNCTION-VALUE-001, because the function-value form is the shape most people reach for.

STILL OPEN: llamagpu headArgmax column walk (needs an in-package benchmark), classic six static equal-chunk row-parallel loops (needs the GOMAXPROCS screen and a forced-serial control first), and the typed-allocator free path that re-boxes a slice header (real, but nothing in production uses that allocator).
